title: Angular Router
description: Angular's built-in router with guards, resolvers, and lazy modules.

data.text: Angular Router is part of @angular/router. It supports guards, resolvers, lazy-loaded modules, and child routes.

data.title: Angular route configuration

data.text: Route Configuration and the Router Outlet

Angular routing is configured as a tree of `Route` objects where each entry matches a path and names the component to render. The `RouterOutlet` directive marks where the matched component goes. A path written with `:name` becomes a parameter read through the `ActivatedRoute` service.

data.title: Routes with a parameter and a lazy module

data.text: `ActivatedRoute` exposes the parameter map as an observable, so the component reacts when the URL changes within the same route. The `Router` service navigates imperatively. Lazy-loaded modules keep the initial bundle small by only fetching code when the route is first visited.

data.title: Subscribe to a route parameter
Lazy loading is the default expectation
data.text: In Angular a large application is split with `loadChildren` so each feature area is its own chunk. Interviewers expect you to explain that this is what keeps the initial bundle small and that the `canActivate` guard is the place to block navigation. Note the guard returns a boolean, an observable, or a `UrlTree` for a redirect.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Guards and resolvers protect and preload routes.
Lazy loading improves initial bundle size.
